nodes.name: Thermal reduction of fcc-PtCo alloy
nodes.procedure: The synthesis and loading of fcc-PtCo alloy were realized by one-step thermal reduction, heating the Pt(II) acetylacetonate, Co(II) acetylacetonate, and support material NC in oleylamine.
nodes.source_text: First, the synthesis and loading of fcc-PtCo alloy were realized by one-step thermal reduction, heating the Pt(II) acetylacetonate, Co(II) acetylacetonate, and support material NC in oleamine.

nodes.name: Annealing to form fct-PtCo
nodes.procedure: After that the alloy was annealed under Ar and H₂ mixed atmosphere to convert the alloy into an ordered (fct-PtCo) and to further couple with the supports, get the catalysts named fct PtCo@NC.
nodes.source_text: After that the alloy was annealed under Ar and H₂ mixed atmosphere to convert the alloy into an ordered (fct-PtCo) and to further couple with the supports

nodes.procedure: High N-doped carbon (HNC) was synthesized and the fct-PtCo@HNC was synthesized from this support using the same method as fct-PtCo@NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: NPs are embedded in NC; fct-PtCo shows highly ordered intermetallic alternating Pt and Co atomic layers with d-spacing of 2.17 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The more precise structural features of fct-PtCo@NC can be seen in high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image (Figure 1c). ... Measurements of lattice spacing show that the d-spacing of fct-PtCo is 2.17 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt and Co elements concentrated on fct-PtCo NPs; N element evenly distributed on support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spatial distributions of Pt, Co, and N were resolved by energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy mapping. As displayed in Figure 1e, the Pt and Co elements are concentrated on fct-PtCo NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atom ratio of Co and Pt is 52%:48%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: from the energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDS) spectrum (Figure S2, Supporting Information), the atom ratio of Co and Pt is 52%:48%.

nodes.characterization_summary: fct-PtCo@NC shows peaks at 41.5°, 47.6°, 54.2°, 60.8°, 69.9° corresponding to (111), (200), (201), (112), (220) planes of fct-PtCo (PDF#43-1358).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obvious peaks on fct-PtCo@NC, fct-PtCo@LNC, and fct-PtCo@rGO at 41.5°, 47.6°, 54.2°, 60.8°, and 69.9°, which correspond to the (111), (200), (201), (112), and (220) crystal planes of fct-PtCo (PDF#43-1358).

nodes.characterization_summary: G band of fct-PtCo@NC gradually blue shifted compared to NC, indicating strong metal-support interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the G band of fcc-PtCo@NC and fct-PtCo@NC is gradually blue shifted, and fct-PtCo@NC shows larger degree of blue shift.

properties.description: Faceted PtCo nanoparticles on nitrogen-doped carbon

nodes.characterization_summary: fct-PtCo@NC shows the lowest work function among catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among the four catalysts, fct-PtCo@NC shows the lowest work function, which means that it has the advantageous structure for charge transfer/transport.

nodes.characterization_summary: fct-PtCo@NC shows blue shifted emission peak and decreased PL intensity compared to NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: compared with NC, a blue shifted emission peak is discovered in fct-PtCo@NC, signifying a band change of NC after loaded PtCo NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC flat band potential -0.54 V; fct-PtCo@NC flat band potential -0.48 V with lower slope.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the flat band potential of NC is -0.54 V ... After loaded fct-PtCo NPs, the flat band potential of fct-PtCo@NC manifests a positive shift (-0.48 V)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p peaks of fct-PtCo@NC show ≈1.38 eV positive shift; Pt 4f peaks show negative shift relative to fct-PtCo@rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the XPS of Co 2p in Figure 2g, compared to fct-PtCo@rGO, the peaks of fct-PtCo@LNC and fct-PtCo@NC exhibit a trend of gradual positive shift. There are ≈1.38 eV positive shift of fct-PtCo@NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: fct-PtCo@NC shows maximum C_dl value of 13.2 mF cm^-2 in alkaline and 13.1 mF cm^-2 in neutral condition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fct-PtCo@NC shows the maximum C_dl value 13.2 and 13.1 mF cm^-2 in alkaline and neutral condition.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA of fct-PtCo@NC is 78.9 m^2 g_Pt^-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the ECSA of fct-PtCo@NC is calculated to be 78.9 m^2 g^-1_Pt

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt content ≈10 wt%; Co:Pt atomic ratio consistent with EDS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt content of fct-PtCo@NC and its control samples all close to 10% . ... the atomic ratio of Co and Pt determined by ICP-MS was consisted with the EDS result.

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad peak between 2800-3500 cm^-1 divided into P1≈3225 cm^-1 (tetrahedral water), P2≈3450 cm^-1 (HER-prone water), P3≈3615 cm^-1 (inactive water); P3 intensity decreases with applied voltage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there is a broad peak between 2800 and 3500 cm^-1 ... this broad peak is divided into three peaks by Gauss fitting, corresponding to tetrahedrally coordinated water (P1≈3225 cm^-1), trihedrally coordinated water (P2≈3450 cm^-1), regarding as the HER-prone water, and interface inactive water (P3≈3615 cm^-1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Absorption peak at 3250 cm^-1 increases with decreasing applied voltage, ascribed to O-H stretching in H3O+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in the FT-IR spectra of fct-PtCo@NC (Figure 4e), there is an absorption peak at 3250 cm^-1 that increases progressively as the applied voltage decreases, which can be ascribed to the stretching vibrations of the O-H group in H3O+.

nodes.characterization_summary: fct-PtCo@NC exhibits the least charge transfer resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fct-PtCo@NC, which with the strong M-S effect, exhibits the least charge transfer resistance among the two pH conditions (Figure S24, Supporting Information).
